title: The perfection of wisdom
hook: the long wisdom sutras, from eight thousand lines to one letter "a"

segments.voice: Yesterday, upaya: a doctor's strange news and a house on fire. Your line was skillful means. Who did you explain something to, and how did your words change? Day one thousand one hundred eleven.

One Mahayana sutra is named for its length: the Perfection of Wisdom in a Hundred Thousand Lines. Another is the Perfection of Wisdom in Eight Thousand Lines. And at the far end of the same family sits a text called the Perfection of Wisdom in One Letter, in which the Buddha gives the whole teaching as a single sound: the letter a. Somewhere in between is a page short enough to read before the kettle boils. Same subject, wildly different sizes. Today, the perfection of wisdom, from long to short.
screen: `A HUNDRED THOUSAND LINES.` → `EIGHT THOUSAND LINES.` → `ONE LETTER.`

segments.voice: First, a family. The perfection of wisdom isn't one book. It's a family of Mahayana sutras with one subject: the wisdom that sees all things as empty of a fixed, separate self, and the bodhisattva who walks the path with that wisdom and with compassion. Which came first, the long ones or the short ones, is a question for historians. Second, why so many sizes. One way to hear it borrows yesterday's word. Some people have the time and the hunger for a hundred thousand lines. Some need a page. Some need one breath. The teaching shrinks or grows to fit whoever is receiving it, the way a doctor fits the dose. Third, the page. The Heart Sutra is the short one this path read slowly in its first year. One of its lines, in plain words, runs: form is emptiness, and emptiness is form. In the sutra's teaching, the things you see and touch are real enough to bump into, and also not solid, separate things standing alone. And that open, connected way things are isn't somewhere else. It's right here, as the cup and the hand and the floor. Fourth, the letter, at the far end of the family. In the One Letter text, the Buddha says the perfection of wisdom is held in the letter a. Some teachers point out that in Sanskrit, a short a at the front of a word can turn it into its opposite: himsa is harm, ahimsa is non-harm. So one small sound can say not to every fixed idea we carry. From a hundred thousand lines down to one letter, the family keeps them all. Only the size of the doorway changes.
screen: `A FAMILY OF SUTRAS.` · `ONE TEACHING, MANY SIZES.` · `FORM IS EMPTINESS.` · `THE WHOLE TEACHING IN A.` · then, large: `FROM LONG TO SHORT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like. Settle, and breathe. Take one line from the Heart Sutra: form is emptiness, emptiness is form. If you have a copy nearby, find the line there; if not, hearing it is enough. Say it once, slowly, in your head. Then look at one thing in front of you, your hand, a cup, the floor, and set the line beside it. Don't try to work it out. Let the line and the thing sit side by side. Then let even the line go, and rest with the breath, short as a single letter. The bell holds the time.
The perfection of wisdom. A family of Mahayana sutras on the wisdom that sees things as they are, from a hundred thousand lines to a single letter. Today's word.
Your line: from long to short. Today, take one long thing you need to say, and find the one-sentence version of it. Tomorrow, mother of the Buddhas. Day one thousand one hundred eleven.

howItsDone: Mahayana communities in East Asia and Tibet chant the Heart Sutra, and some monasteries read or recite the longer perfection of wisdom sutras on special days.

fork.setup: you want the perfection of wisdom. you're offered the sutra in a hundred thousand lines, the page-long Heart Sutra, or the single letter a. which one holds the teaching?
options: only the longest; the short ones leave things out
only the shortest; the long ones are padding
all of them; the doorway changes size, not the wisdom
fork.reveal: the family keeps them all, long and short, as one perfection of wisdom fitted to different readers.

original.note: Sanskrit: the short a, the one letter in which, in one sutra, the whole perfection of wisdom is given.

trapdoor: what you thought: one long, difficult book.
what it means: a family of Mahayana sutras on the wisdom that sees things as they are, told at lengths from vast to a single letter.
what a scholar hears: prajnaparamita literature, from the Eight Thousand Lines to the Heart Sutra and the One Letter, one teaching at many sizes.

notes: Numbers in this script (a hundred thousand lines, eight thousand lines, one letter) are only the titles of the texts themselves.
'Form is emptiness, and emptiness is form' is given as a plain-words paraphrase, not a quotation; Müller's 1894 translation (SBE XLIX) is not on the validator's list.

The One Letter text: confirm that the Buddha says the perfection of wisdom is contained in the letter a. The ahimsa note (a negating prefix) is grammar, attributed to 'some teachers' as a reading of why a; a Keeper may prefer to cut the interpretation.
'Which came first ... is a question for historians' deliberately avoids stating an order or dates.
Day 1112 (the mother of the Buddhas, already written by another writer) takes the name prajnaparamita and the mother image; this day avoids both.
howItsDone: 'some monasteries read or recite the longer sutras on special days' (e.g. the Tibetan reading of the Prajnaparamita); confirm.

Editor: 'its best-known line' (an unsourced superlative) changed to 'one of its lines'; the account of form and emptiness is now framed as 'in the sutra's teaching' so the narrator does not assert it.
